Green: proof/VELDO-0306/suite-green.txt.

The rows run the adapter against a real Ledger on a real control store, and send run finished through the real Signal, kind registry, probes, safety rules and removers; the project is in act mode by the owner's own signed command with a real key. The event stream is the output pipe of a real child process, waited on with the kernel's select and handed to the Service class's own docker_readable. Row integration/real-engine ran on this host against the real engine (context default; engine 29.2.1 as recorded at the build and the review, 29.3.0 in the run of the fix from the second review) with objects the row itself created under names made for that run: a labelled volume, network and container and an unlabelled volume were recorded from the real inspect records, a labelled container created after the engine's time was read and before the subscription became an item from the event the engine printed again (--since), the event client was started with the row's own label as a filter, the labelled ones were removed at run finished by the real client, through the row's client that passes only a stop or a remove of an object the row created, in the order container, network, volume, the unlabelled volume stayed as a report, the row's client refused nothing, and the row left none of its objects behind; the lists of the host's containers, volumes and networks were the same before and after (suite-green.txt). assumptions: 1. THE ENGINE OF THE ROWS IS A STAND-IN, a class in the suite that holds containers, networks and volumes for two contexts and refuses as an engine does without a force option. Only integration/real-engine asks a real engine, and it runs only where the docker client answers on the context default or desktop-linux with an image there, and never under a mutant; in the gate's confinement it prints a SELFTEST SKIP line and adds no row, so the gate does not prove it. It ran green on the build host. Its procedure also runs on a second stand-in in every run.

2. NOTHING SETS Service.space_docker YET. The service has no space ledger of its own, so no adapter is built for it in this repository: the pipes are in the poll set from the moment a later ticket sets the attribute. The loop of serve is not driven by a row; its select is read from its source (ac4/poll-set), and the rows call the Service class's own docker_pipes and docker_readable on a namespace that holds the adapter.

3. A RUN IS NOT GIVEN ITS LABEL YET. Putting the space label and the compose project name in a run's environment is the receiver's (design 6.3) and is not in this ticket's footprint; control_space_docker.given says what the two are. The rows label their objects themselves. Other stand-ins: the two checks of a switch to act (VELDO-0332, 0339), the process table (an empty fixture folder), the client that prints events (a real cat process).

4. THE FOOTPRINT GREW by control_space_signal.py and control_space_probe.py with their synced copies, for rule 1: it knew a Docker object by its engine Id alone, an engine gives a volume no Id, and so no volume could go at run finished. Rule 1 now passes a volume whose locator holds created_at when the engine shows a volume made at that time. Neither file is a protected path. The spec's History records it; it is the lead's to confirm.
5. IMAGES ARE NOT READ (VELDO-0328), and the adoption rule by compose's working folder and by bind source is VELDO-0307. An object those would give an owner is a report here.

6. A VOLUME'S IDENTITY IS ITS CreatedAt, which an engine gives to the second (the residual VELDO-0300 names): a volume removed and made again inside the same second under the same name is not told apart by it. Such a volume still has to carry the run's label or compose name to be the run's.

7. SEEN AND NOT CHANGED: control_space_probe.located takes "no such" in a client's words for the engine's answer that an object is absent. A real engine says "network <name> not found", so Signal defers a network removed by hand as not_in_ledger and never marks it gone (nothing is lost by that). The adapter reads the engine's own answer for each kind (absent).

8. THE REVIEW'S FIX (findings 1 to 5) IS IN THIS BUNDLE; the spec's History says what each changed. The four .veldo files of the fix (control_space_docker.py, control_service.py, control_space_probe.py, control_space_signal.py) are in commit fe486efb (VELDO-0305, review): the run fixing VELDO-0305 in the same worktree took them into its commit while this fix was in progress, before their engine copies were synced. Commit 9e479e21 holds the synced engine copies, the last two lines of control_space_signal.py, the suite, the driver, the suite manifest and the spec. At fe486efb alone the template-sync check is red; at 9e479e21 it passes.

9. THE ROW'S LABEL FILTER LETS NO VOLUME EVENT THROUGH: an engine puts a container's labels in its events and a volume's and a network's in none. So the object the real-engine row makes for its event is a container. The adapter of the service asks for no label filter: it reads every event of the three types.

10. A CONTAINER THAT MOUNTS A PROTECTED PATH IS JUDGED BY THE BIND SOURCE AS THE ENGINE SHOWS IT, at, above or beneath a protected path, read plainly and through links on this host. An engine on another host or in a machine of its own (a desktop engine) may show a source this host reads differently; such a container is then judged by its volumes and its own name and compose project alone. While any compose project is protected on an engine, each mounted volume is asked for once more (one inspect a volume) at each record and each removal.

11. THE TIME OF THE SUBSCRIPTION IS THE ENGINE'S OWN, read through its client; the engine prints again every event from that time on, so an object recorded by the snapshot is asked for once more and writes nothing. An engine whose time cannot be read is down and is said so; nothing starts it again but start().

12. NOT FIXED HERE: the review's notes for the lead (nothing sets Service.space_docker yet; suites 127 and 86 not rerun). Service.docker_unread is there for reconcile and the console to read; neither reads it yet (VELDO-0315).

13. FROM THE SECOND REVIEW (N1): only path entries are read whatever engines they name. A volume or a compose project entry is still read by engine, as the protect list declares them. The suite now loads control_space_probe.py through its PRODUCTION map, so the real-engine row's guard compares the probe with its canon too. The real-engine row ran on this host in the run of this fix (context default); it binds no protected path, and the new row is on the stand-in engine only.
rollback: Revert the change. Docker objects are neither recorded nor removed by Veldo.
